about: One card per experiment, in the shape the UAT review asked for (section 5.1): what changed, the problem, the hypothesis, the measure, the result, what we learned, the decision and when to revisit. The Log tab reads it. New log entries add a card here.

cards.title: Vocal review mark on setup D (rule V)
cards.problem: Vocals leak into setup D's sax stem on pop records and get written as sax (Austin's Najee and Burning Daylight flags; step 1 diagnosis).
cards.hypothesis: Marking notes where the Demucs vocal stem is louder than the sax stem at the note's pitch catches leaked vocals without marking real sax.
cards.changed: A review mark only (rule V), nothing hidden; round 2 added a same-line gate on the vocal and sax spectra.
cards.measure: Good marks (extras, notes in key rests) against bad marks (notes matching the key); marks inside vs outside Austin's not-sax flags.
cards.result: Picked vocals ≥ 0 dB: Austin's 6 tunes 139 good, 218 bad (8.3%), mostly on Pennies and Blues for Mary Jane; Najee 228/603 marked inside flags vs 31/528 outside.
cards.learned: Demucs routes the sax into its vocals stem on instrumentals. A pick set with no vocals can't reward a vocal gate.
cards.decision: Not adopted. Next is Austin's choice: Mega vocals (round 3) or a vocal tuning set first.
cards.revisit: With a cleaner vocal stem (Mega vocals, becruily deux, BS Roformer 124) and a pick set that has vocals.

cards.title: Benchmark re-score: six versions on 33 trusted songs
cards.problem: E80 picked today's default on only 9 songs (ADR-0041's worry).
cards.hypothesis: Setup D's lead over the standard path holds on a benchmark three times the size, in every group of songs.
cards.changed: Nothing in the tool: four milestone versions (#9, #35, #57, #81) and today's two paths (A standard, D our sax model) re-scored on the same songs.
cards.measure: Note F1, onset F1 and notes per key note; 33 songs (24 transcribed, Austin's 6, 3 Parker test records).
cards.result: Note F1 32.1, 35.9, 37.5, 38.8 for the milestones, A 39.7, D 50.9. D wins 31 of 33; 12 songs at 60 or above (A 2).
cards.learned: Step-by-step changes added about 8 points; switching to D added 11 in one step. Three keys were an octave off and were fixed.
cards.decision: Keep D as the band-record default. The benchmark is the yardstick for later changes.
cards.revisit: When a new default or a new benchmark version arrives.

cards.title: Our fine-tuned note finder in the app path: four setups
cards.problem: E77's fine-tuned finder was only tested on Mega stems, not the way the app runs.
cards.hypothesis: Filosax separator plus our finder (D) beats the standard path (A) on Austin's tunes and the Parker test records.
cards.changed: Four setups: A standard, B Demucs + our finder, C Demucs + original Filosax finder, D Filosax separator + our finder.
cards.measure: Note F1 on austin-6 and the Parker test records.
cards.result: D beat A on all 9 songs: austin-6 37.7 → 45.7, Parker test 56.6 → 69.9. Notes per key note 1.32 → 1.04.
cards.learned: Most of D's gain comes from the pretrained Filosax parts; our fine-tune adds about 5 points.
cards.decision: Adopted: D is the band-record default in the app (ADR-0041, build PR #147).
cards.revisit: Nine songs is small: confirmed by E81.

cards.title: Sax judge: is a sax playing, and which one?
cards.problem: The not-sax checks and training-track screening need a second opinion on whether, and which, sax is playing.
cards.hypothesis: A small probe on a large pretrained music model can tell sax from not-sax and alto from tenor.
cards.changed: Probes on frozen MERT and MuQ, trained on keyed records plus single-note libraries.
cards.measure: AUC for sax playing on held-out windows; records whose sax type is called right.
cards.result: MERT AUC 0.93 against MuQ 0.80; sax type right on 63 of 64 records. Soprano fails.
cards.learned: Not-sax windows are only 3% of the data and soprano has no band examples.
cards.decision: MERT is the judge to use; not wired in yet.
cards.revisit: Once more not-sax and soprano examples exist, as a vote in the not-sax checks.

cards.title: Fine-tuning the Filosax note finder on Mega sax stems
cards.problem: Mega's stem holds the quiet notes but the note finder misses them (E73, E74).
cards.hypothesis: Training on sax-in-band stems raises note F1 on unseen players by 5 points or more.
cards.changed: filosax_25k fine-tuned on E76's 110 Mega-separated solo spans; checkpoint from step 2,488 kept.
cards.measure: Note F1 on Austin's six tunes, the Parker test records and three held-out players.
cards.result: Six tunes 43.3 → 48.0, Parker test 63.7 → 69.3, held-out players +7 to +10. Notes per key note 1.07 → 0.98.
cards.learned: Gains everywhere but Walker's Theme. The held-out players also chose the checkpoint, so their gains are slightly optimistic.
cards.decision: Kept; became the default's note finder after E80.
cards.revisit: Second fine-tune on cleaner tracks once the sax judge and a better separator are ready.

cards.title: Training set for the note finder
cards.problem: No sax-in-band training data with note labels.
cards.hypothesis: Keyed Weimar and Parker records separated with Mega give labels that line up with the stems.
cards.changed: 134 solo spans (about 300 minutes) separated with Mega; Coltrane, Potter and Getz held out.
cards.measure: Every stem present and not silent; label-to-stem fit.
cards.result: Median key note 25 dB above its neighbours; 110 spans for training.

cards.title: Answer keys from Austin's 8 transcription PDFs
cards.problem: The test sets lacked the modern and ballad playing Austin cares about.
cards.changed: Seven printed transcriptions read with homr and lined up with the records.
cards.measure: Note F1, note F1 ignoring note ends, onset F1, pitch, and key agreement.
cards.result: Baseline note F1 21.5 (37.3 ignoring note ends).
cards.learned: Free time and ballads score lowest even where the key fits; note ends and onsets are the weak part, not pitch.

cards.title: Alto etude answer keys: Ferling and Luft
cards.problem: No written-music test on real alto takes.
cards.changed: 52 alto takes with keys read from public-domain scans.
cards.measure: Note F1 and its parts on the standard solo path.
cards.result: Note F1 57.5 overall: fast studies 70.0, slow studies 39.1.
cards.learned: Slow studies lose to held notes split by vibrato; onset recall is high (83%).
cards.decision: No change. A vibrato-aware held-note fix would need Austin's go.

cards.title: Note-finder settings on Mega sax stems
cards.problem: Mega's stem holds almost every key note, yet the note finders write far fewer (E73).
cards.hypothesis: Different thresholds on Mega stems close the gap.
cards.changed: Thresholds tuned on the Parker training records for both note finders.
cards.measure: Note F1, note F1 ignoring note ends, onset F1 on the test set.
cards.result: Filosax finder 54.4 → 54.6; Basic Pitch's shipped settings already best.
cards.learned: The misses are timing, scooped pitch and merged repeats, which thresholds can't fix.
cards.decision: Rejected. Led to fine-tuning our own finder (E76, E77).

cards.title: How many key notes each separator's stem holds
cards.problem: Is the missing quiet sax lost in separation or in note finding?
cards.changed: Stems measured alone, before any note finder.
cards.measure: Share of key notes held in the stem; leakage during a piano solo.
cards.result: Mega holds 57 of Austin's 59 flagged notes (Filosax 40) and leaks least (−77 dB against −16 dB).
cards.learned: The remaining gap is the note finder.
cards.revisit: Mega as the separator for D is the current challenger.

cards.title: Start a note on a pitch change without an attack
cards.problem: Slurred notes looked missed in E70.
cards.hypothesis: Starting a note where the pitch switches without an attack catches them.
cards.changed: New rule on the Filosax path: frame threshold 0.7, at least 60 ms.
cards.measure: Note F1 on the test set; notes found in Austin's flagged bars.
cards.result: Note F1 unchanged at 65.1; flagged bars still 18 of 59.
cards.learned: The 'slurs' were right-pitch notes placed 100–190 ms off, or missing from the stem.
cards.revisit: On setup D (judged on the old Filosax path).

cards.title: Layered separation: stacking separators
cards.problem: The Filosax separator loses quiet sax (E69, E70).
cards.hypothesis: Passing the audio through several separators in turn gives a cleaner, fuller sax stem.
cards.changed: Four variants: Filosax, Mega sax on the mix, Demucs → Mega sax, Demucs → wind → sax.
cards.measure: Note F1 and its parts; key notes found in Austin's flagged bars.
cards.result: Mega on the mix best on test (54.4 against 53.3); stacking added nothing; per record mixed.
cards.learned: Mega alone is as good as any stack; slow, about 3 minutes per minute of audio.
cards.decision: Stacked variants dropped; Mega offered as an opt-in.

cards.title: Recovering the quiet low notes on the Filosax path
cards.problem: Austin flagged quiet low notes as missing (E69).
cards.hypothesis: A more sensitive finder below D5, or borrowing standard-path notes where the stem drops, recovers them.
cards.changed: Fix A (borrow notes) and fix B (more sensitive below D5).
cards.measure: Note F1, low notes found, extra notes, notes in rests.
cards.result: No gain: note F1 65.1 → 64.9; flagged bars stay at 18 of 59.
cards.learned: 31 of 41 misses get almost no note-start signal: lost at separation.
cards.revisit: On setup D (judged on the old Filosax path).
